Permutation Significance Testing for Cross-Network Structural Differences

Source: R/stat_network_permutation.R
cli_network_permutation.Rd

Evaluates whether global topological structural metrics (edge density, natural connectivity, negative-to-positive edge ratio, mean degree, and clustering coefficient) differ significantly between experimental conditions (e.g. KO vs WT, Case vs Control, or Healthy vs Lesional). Generates an empirical null distribution by shuffling sample group labels \(B\) times, recomputing correlation networks, and calculating two-sided permutation p-values.

Usage

cli_network_permutation(
  comm_data,
  group,
  ref_group = NULL,
  test_group = NULL,
  cor_method = c("spearman", "pearson"),
  cor_cutoff = 0.35,
  p_cutoff = 0.05,
  n_perm = 199,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

comm_data

Numeric matrix or data frame of feature abundances (samples in rows, features in columns).

group

Factor or character vector specifying condition assignments for each sample. Must match nrow(comm_data) and contain at least 2 distinct groups.

ref_group

Optional character string designating the baseline reference group. If NULL, the first level of group is used.

test_group

Optional character string designating the comparison group. If NULL, the second level of group is used.

cor_method

Correlation metric: "spearman" (default) or "pearson".

cor_cutoff

Absolute correlation threshold \(|r|\) to establish network edges (default 0.35).

p_cutoff

Significance threshold for correlation p-values (default 0.05).

n_perm

Integer. Number of permutation iterations (default 199).

seed

Optional integer seed for reproducibility.

Value

A data frame summarizing observed metrics, permuted null means, standard errors, and two-sided permutation p-values:

metric

Topological network metric

ref_val

Observed metric value in the reference condition

test_val

Observed metric value in the test condition

delta_obs

Observed difference (test_val - ref_val)

perm_mean

Mean of the permuted null differences

perm_se

Standard error of the permuted null differences

p_perm

Two-sided empirical permutation p-value

Examples

set.seed(42)
comm <- matrix(rpois(40 * 25, lambda = 12), nrow = 40, ncol = 25)
colnames(comm) <- paste0("Taxon_", 1:25)
grp <- rep(c("Control", "Treatment"), each = 20)
perm_res <- cli_network_permutation(comm, grp, n_perm = 49, seed = 42)
print(perm_res)
#> 
#> =================================================================
#>  cliomicplot: Cross-Network Permutation Test
#>  Reference (Control) vs Comparison (Treatment)
#>  Number of Permutations: 49
#> =================================================================
#>                   metric ref_val test_val delta_obs perm_mean perm_se p_perm
#>             Edge Density  0.0500   0.0500    0.0000   -0.0034  0.0228   1.00
#>     Natural Connectivity  0.5612   0.5761    0.0149   -0.0333  0.3004   0.96
#>  Negative/Positive Ratio  0.5000   0.5000    0.0000    0.0141  0.4859   1.00
#>              Mean Degree  1.2000   1.2000    0.0000   -0.0816  0.5461   1.00
#>   Clustering Coefficient  0.0000   0.0000    0.0000    0.0027  0.1197   1.00
#> -----------------------------------------------------------------
#>  Note: Two-sided empirical p-value: (1 + sum(|delta_null| >= |delta_obs|)) / (B + 1)
#>
